solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wonder about computer system — it shows astonishing quality

indicators.note: one word lying about others wraps itself around them

parts.note: a prodigy is a wonder, a marvel
iOS is Apple's operating system
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at a computer system that displays an amazing feature.
explanation.walkthrough: iOS is Apple's operating system for phones and tablets; the little word it is used just as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigiosity is the state of being prodigious, an amazing or marvellous character.

clue.text: Continue working perhaps around bottom switch

indicators.note: the phrase for keeping going is placed around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to press on is to carry on working, one example of continuing
butt is slang for the bottom

explanation.surface: Advice to keep working, perhaps after flicking a switch under something.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-button is a switch worked by pressing, a push-button control.

clue.text: Long-distance motor race really disorganised

indicators.note: something disorganised is in a muddle, so its letters are out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a long car race was badly organised.
explanation.definitionFit: A rallye is a motor rally, a long-distance road race for cars.

clue.text: Model Danielle needing Chanel's latest dress material, originally wool

indicators.note: to model is to shape something into a new form
needing means lacking, so that letter is missing from the name

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the latest of a word is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of Chanel

explanation.surface: A model named Danielle wants a Chanel dress in wool.
explanation.walkthrough: One L comes out of DANIELLE, and the seven letters left are rearranged into DELAINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaine, from French mousseline de laine, is a light dress fabric first made of wool.

clue.text: Cavalry regiment is pressing outside bank

indicators.note: the first piece sits on the outside of the second, wrapping it

parts.note: someone who is pressing clothes irons them
a bank is the side of a river or hill

explanation.surface: A cavalry unit applies pressure around the flank of a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is pressing' reads as urgent; it is someone doing the ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironsides was the name of Cromwell's cavalry troopers in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Democrat emerging more shaky and rather unpleasant

indicators.note: the party member emerging means leaving the word, so that letter goes

parts.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, as a dicky heart
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A Democrat politician comes out looking shakier and rather nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: DICKIER loses its D. Dicky is British slang for weak or unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Icky means sickly or distasteful, so ickier is a comparative of unpleasant.

clue.text: Former Indian PM missing government function

indicators.note: missing means going without, so that letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Manmohan Singh was prime minister of India from 2004 to 2014
G is the abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: An ex-prime minister of India is absent from a government role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a role or event; here it is the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinh is the hyperbolic sine, a mathematical function.

clue.text: Rendered herein as "plant"

indicators.note: to render is to translate or recast, so the letters are put into another form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A translator notes that the word here was given as plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like the word being translated; it is a slang verb for bury.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhearse, a Shakespearean word, means to place in a hearse or coffin, i.e. to bury, slangily to plant.

clue.text: Third time for parking in Jag

indicators.note: one thing stands for another, taking its place in the word

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
to jag is to prick or pierce

explanation.surface: Third time someone has left a Jaguar car in a parking spot.
explanation.walkthrough: In PIERCE the P is swapped for T. 'Jag' looks like the car; it is a verb meaning stab.
explanation.definitionFit: Tierce is an old word for a third, also the third canonical hour and a fencing position.

clue.text: Stock cut? Could be rootstock as before

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lineage, breed or descent
second meaning: an archaic word for a root, as a root of ginger

explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' flags the old sense, from Shakespeare's 'a race of ginger'. 'Cut' may hint at the ginger root being a cut piece; it gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a breed or lineage, and in older English also a root of ginger, so it fits both.

clue.text: With focus on means private hospital is unbending

parts.note: the old preposition a means on, as in abed and ashore
a clinic is a private hospital

explanation.surface: A private hospital being described as inflexible.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter reads the little word a in its sense 'on'; the surface makes 'means' look like money.
explanation.definitionFit: Aclinic means without inclination, used of a line where a compass needle has no dip, so not bending.

clue.text: Cooking roles changed in housing

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the next

parts.note: a casing is a housing, an outer cover

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the order of those letters is altered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Household chores swapped around, a cook trading jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Casseroling is cooking slowly in a covered dish, a casserole.

clue.text: Tangled hair shown by the Spanish troops

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
troops as a verb means moves in crowds, as flocks does

explanation.surface: Unkempt hair on Spanish soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Elflocks are tangled locks of hair, as if knotted by elves; the term comes from Shakespeare.

clue.text: In Scotland slight lead for Sturgeon getting credit

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Sturgeon
a loan is credit extended

explanation.surface: In Scottish politics, Nicola Sturgeon has a narrow lead and receives praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicola Sturgeon was Scotland's First Minister, which sets the Scottish scene; the fish name gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloan is a Scots word for a snub or slight.

clue.text: Loud laughter coming from Republican in recesses

indicators.note: in places the party letter inside the next word

parts.note: niches are recesses in a wall
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Raucous laughter heard from a Republican hiding in alcoves.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicher is a neigh or loud snigger, chiefly Scots, so nichers are bursts of laughter.

clue.text: Rejecting lead, French school supports campaign for lead-free air? That's stuff glossed over

indicators.note: rejecting the lead means turning away the front letter
in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the other

parts.note: CLEAR, the Campaign for Lead-Free Air, pressed for unleaded petrol in Britain
école is French for school

explanation.surface: Ecologists campaigning against leaded petrol, backed by a French school.
explanation.walkthrough: ECOLE drops its first letter to leave COLE, which goes under CLEAR. The word 'lead' appears twice with different jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearcole is a size or priming coat painted on before gilding or paint is applied over it.

clue.text: Special fastenings to stop vessel that's large? Actually largest

indicators.note: to stop a vessel is to plug it, so these pieces fill its middle

parts.note: a vat is a large vessel
S is the abbreviation for special
ties are fastenings

explanation.surface: Special clamps to seal a huge container.
explanation.walkthrough: Vasty is Shakespeare's word for vast, so the question-and-answer tail of the clue moves from the plain adjective to its superlative.
explanation.definitionFit: Vastiest is the superlative of vasty, an archaic form of vast, so it means largest.

clue.text: Beat all chess records from years ago

indicators.note: to beat something is to batter it out of shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of beating every chess record set long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Records' looks like best performances at chess; it means old gramophone discs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellacs were 78 rpm gramophone records, made of shellac before vinyl replaced them.

clue.text: Runner starts in international eschewing a hat

parts.note: a runner is a climbing bean, the runner bean

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

parts.note: first letters of international and eschewing

explanation.surface: An international athlete takes to the track without headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like an athlete; it is the bean.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanie is a small close-fitting knitted cap.

clue.text: Wicked spirit shown in one hour overseeing main suspect

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour
taken as written

explanation.surface: An evil spirit appears for an hour supervising the chief suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, overseeing means sitting above, so the first pieces come before the shuffled word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahriman is the evil spirit, the destructive power, in Zoroastrian religion.

clue.text: Again gold for French actor

parts.note: more means again, once more
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A French performer wins gold again.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeanne Moreau was a celebrated French film actress, star of Jules et Jim.

clue.text: Devotee holds tip of rose bud

indicators.note: holds means grips, so one word clasps the letter inside it

parts.note: a fiend is a devotee or fanatic, as a fresh-air fiend

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of rose

explanation.surface: A keen gardener grasps the end of a rosebud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose bud' reads as one flower; bud is slang for a pal and stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Bud, short for buddy, is a mate or companion.

clue.text: American novelist backed less good swimmer

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the name runs from end to start
less means minus, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: John Grisham is an American writer of legal thrillers
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: An American author supported a fish that is not much good.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversed GRISHAM is MAHSIRG, and dropping the G leaves MAHSIR.
explanation.definitionFit: The mahsir, or mahseer, is a large freshwater game fish of India, so a swimmer.

clue.text: Sort of transfer club agreed upon

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
on means agreed, as in 'the deal is on'

explanation.surface: A football club settles a player transfer deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transfer' looks like a football deal; it is a design applied with an iron.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron-on transfer is a printed design fixed to fabric by ironing.

clue.text: One staggering sum shorter after section removed

parts.note: a tot is a sum, an addition

indicators.note: removed means taken out, so that letter goes

parts.note: terser means shorter, more concise
S is the abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: A shocking total that came out lower once one part was cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggering' reads as astonishing beside sum; it is the definition, meaning tottering.
explanation.definitionFit: A totterer is one who walks unsteadily, staggering.

clue.text: Massage is needed after more than one fall

parts.note: trips are stumbles, several falls
taken as written

explanation.surface: A massage is required after taking several tumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripsis is the medical term for massage or rubbing, a kneading treatment.

clue.text: Old Jack arrests one that's bad up north

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold someone, so one word holds another

parts.note: pur was the old name for the knave or jack in the card game post and pair
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An old sailor detains a wrongdoer in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: PUR holds I. Jack looks like a sailor; it is a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: Puir is the Scots form of poor, here in its sense of bad or inferior.

clue.text: Spring onion cooked primarily with poor second-class oil

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: first letter of cooked

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: B is the grade for second class
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spring onion fried in cheap, second-rate oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Cibol is an old name for the Welsh onion, a kind of spring onion or scallion.

clue.text: Guys love small whitefish found in Canada

parts.note: guys are men
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
mini means small

explanation.surface: Men who enjoy small fish caught in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: The menominee or menomini is a round whitefish of North American lakes, including Canada's.

clue.text: Bridge points are occupying partners, indeed concerning South

indicators.note: to occupy a space is to sit inside it

parts.note: North and South are partners at bridge
an are is a unit of area, abbreviated A
I is an old spelling of ay, yes, so indeed
on means about, concerning
S is the abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: A bridge scoring note about partners and the South hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' looks like the card game, and partners fits it; the definition is the bridge of the nose. An are is a metric unit of land area.
explanation.definitionFit: The nasion is the anatomical point where the bridge of the nose meets the forehead.

clue.text: Overturned old car in the river

indicators.note: a car overturned lies upside down, so in a word the order is flipped

parts.note: the Vauxhall Nova was a small car of the 1980s and 1990s

explanation.surface: An old car flipped over and ended up in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avon is an English river, the one at Stratford; avon is also Welsh for river.

clue.text: Blush applied during excursion is winning with colour

indicators.note: something applied during an event is put in the middle of it

parts.note: an outing is an excursion
to blush is to redden

explanation.surface: Someone puts on blusher during a day trip and looks winningly rosy.
explanation.definitionFit: To outredden is to surpass in redness, so outreddening is beating others for colour.
